title: Structure-aware chunking
summary: Parse the document's own structure (headings, sections, tables, layout) and split along it, keeping the section path as metadata. Chunks follow the author's meaning, not a token counter.
useIf: Documents have headings, tables or layout and answers live inside sections you can name.
avoidIf: The text is flat, or the parser cannot recover headings reliably, so the structure you split on is wrong.

explain.md: **Structure-aware chunking** splits on what the author already marked: markdown headings, HTML tags, layout blocks, list items, tables. The chunker walks the heading tree and emits a chunk per section. A table or code block is kept as one unit. If a section is longer than the limit, a recursive splitter divides it, and short sibling sections can be merged up. Each chunk records its **section path**, for example `Returns > International > Import duties`.

explain.title: Structure-aware pipeline
explain.alt: A document is parsed into structured markdown, split by heading tree, oversized sections are split recursively, tables are kept whole, and each chunk receives a section path.
explain.src:
flowchart LR
  A["Document"] --> B["Parse to markdown or layout"]
  B --> C["Split by heading tree"]
  C --> D["Keep tables and code whole"]
  D --> E["Cap size inside long sections"]
  E --> F["Attach section path"]

explain.md: The quality of the split depends on the parse. Document Intelligence layout v4.0 returns Markdown with headings, HTML tables, handwriting flags and figure regions [[tr41]]. The AI Search Content Understanding skill extracts and chunks in one step, with a default chunk length of 500 and a range of 300 to 50,000 characters or 100 to 8,000 tokens [[tr5]]. The Azure Architecture Center advises matching the approach to the document type (structured, semi-structured, unstructured) and shows a Content Understanding analyzer that adds title, summary and keywords as chunk metadata [[tr9]].

explain.caption: Metadata worth storing with every structure-aware chunk
head: Field
Why it earns its place
rows: Disambiguates the chunk, supports filters and citations
Enables window expansion and page-level citations
Lets you route or weight chunk types
Supports updates and deletes by document
Every chunk must inherit its document's permissions

explain.title: Section path: field or prepended text?
explain.md: Prepending the path to the chunk text makes it searchable and visible to the embedding, but adds tokens to every chunk. Storing it in a separate field costs nothing in the embedding but is not matched unless you search that field. Many teams do both for a short path.

The chunk visualizer lab in the fixed-size chunking topic shows the difference on a markdown document with a table. Compare 'Fixed 64 on markdown' with 'Structure-aware 64': the second keeps the table whole at the price of uneven chunk sizes.

whereToUse: Policy manuals, product documentation, specifications and wikis with real headings
Reports and slide decks parsed by a layout model into markdown
Sources that need citations by section or per-section permissions
Documents with tables or code where splitting mid-block destroys meaning

use: Answers are scoped to a named section
You want stable chunk boundaries under edits
avoid: Flat text with no usable structure
Scanned files where heading detection is unreliable and unchecked
Sections vary from one line to many pages with no size cap
flips: Parser quality is poor: fix parsing first or fall back to recursive splitting
Sections are huge: add a size cap and parent-child retrieval
Questions cross sections: retrieve parents or neighbouring sections

pitfalls.symptom: Some sections are one line, others twenty pages
pitfalls.cause: Splitting strictly on headings produces uneven sizes
pitfalls.fix: Merge small siblings up to a minimum and recursively split large sections to a maximum

pitfalls.symptom: A scanned PDF yields one giant chunk
pitfalls.cause: OCR text has no detected headings, so the heading splitter finds nothing
pitfalls.fix: Use layout analysis that detects headings, verify on a sample, and fall back to recursive splitting

pitfalls.symptom: Parsing code breaks after a Document Intelligence version change
pitfalls.cause: In v4.0 `2024-11-30` Markdown tables are HTML tables and checkboxes use the symbols ☒ and ☐ instead of `:selected:` and `:unselected:`
pitfalls.fix: Pin the API version and re-run a parsing regression set on upgrade

scenarios.title: Policy manuals with per-section access
scenarios.situation: An assistant answers from internal policy manuals. Each section can have its own audience and users expect citations that name the section. The files are born-digital with real headings.
unknowns: Do permissions vary inside a document?
How long are the longest sections?
scenarios.question: How do you chunk?

options.name: Split by heading tree, cap at about 512 tokens, store section path and access fields on each chunk
options.why: Sections map to meaning, citations are exact and permissions attach to the right unit.
options.tradeoff: Uneven chunk sizes and a dependency on clean headings.

options.name: Recursive splitting at 512 tokens
options.why: Simple and tolerant of missing headings.
options.tradeoff: Citations lose the section name unless you reattach it.

options.name: Fixed 512 tokens with 25% overlap over the whole file
options.why: Chunks span section edges, so one chunk can mix audiences and cite no section.
options.tradeoff: Right only for flat text with no headings.

flips.then: Normalise headings in the parse step or fall back to recursive splitting per source.
Add parent-child retrieval so small children match and sections are returned.

scenarios.takeaway: When structure carries meaning and permissions, split along it and record it.

scenarios.title: Scanned contracts, unknown layout quality
scenarios.situation: A legal team archives scanned contracts. Some have clean numbered clauses and others are skewed or handwritten. The team needs clause-level retrieval.
unknowns: What share of scans is poor?
scenarios.question: What is the first step?

options.name: Run layout analysis to markdown, validate heading and clause detection on a sample, then split structurally with a recursive fallback
options.why: Structure only exists after parsing, so quality is checked before splitting.
options.tradeoff: Parsing cost and a manual review loop.

options.name: Fixed 512 tokens with 15% overlap on raw OCR text
options.tradeoff: Clauses are cut at arbitrary points.

options.name: A markdown-header splitter on raw OCR text
options.why: Raw OCR has no markdown headings to find, so it emits giant chunks.
options.tradeoff: Right once a layout model has produced markdown.

flips.then: Route those to a vision-based parser or accept the fixed-size fallback.

flips.if: Volume is huge and cost bites
flips.then: Parse only documents that users actually query first.

scenarios.takeaway: Structure-aware chunking is only as good as the parse that feeds it.

quiz.q: Structure-aware chunking over scanned PDFs yields huge chunks with no section paths. Most likely cause?
options: The embedding model is too small
OCR output has no detected headings to split on
quiz.explain: Without headings in the parsed text, a heading-based splitter has nothing to split on. Model size, overlap and similarity metric do not affect heading splitting.

quiz.q: Which are real costs of splitting strictly by heading?
quiz.explain: Section sizes vary and the split is only as good as the parse. Mid-sentence cuts come from blind splitting, and a section path is a benefit of this strategy, not a loss.

quiz.q: Match each metadata field to the job it does.

pairs.r: Disambiguates a chunk and supports section citations
Routes or weights text, table, figure and code chunks

quiz.explain: Each field answers a specific need: context, neighbour lookup, routing and security trimming. All four must be stored at ingest because they cannot be reconstructed from the vector.

flashcards.front: What does a structure-aware chunker split on?
flashcards.back: Headings, layout blocks, tables and code, usually from markdown or a layout parse, with a size cap and merging of small sections.

flashcards.front: What is a section path and why store it?
flashcards.back: The heading trail, such as Returns > International > Duties. It disambiguates the chunk, supports citations and filters.

flashcards.front: What changed in Document Intelligence v4.0 `2024-11-30` Markdown output?
flashcards.back: Tables are returned as HTML tables and checkboxes use the symbols ☒ and ☐ instead of the older selected tokens.
